summary: Frontend-only verification of the redesigned Purchase Order Creation page (/purchasing-strategy/purchase-order-create) using the synthetic vms_session cookie. Ran 3 Playwright suites covering: page/layout render + all spec data-testids, site->company auto-derivation (P1->RI, P2->RT), Bill-To scoping/reset, supplier live search + payment-terms badge, product live search + UoM autofill, line math (Qty*Price), sidebar Total Units/Gross Order Value, Add Item / duplicate / remove (disabled at 1 row), checklist orange<->green transitions, submit-button gating, incomplete-form toast path, and the Confirm dialog audit recap (Cancel only - 'Confirm & Submit' was NEVER clicked, no SAP write performed). Backend skipped per request. All functional logic is intact after the redesign.

issues: PO Date (po-date-input) and per-line Delivery Date (po-line-delivery-date-input-{idx}) use the native browser date picker (mm/dd/yyyy spinner) instead of the shadcn Calendar/Popover component; visually inconsistent with the rest of the tactical design. Pre-existing, low priority.

Sticky sidebar uses `sticky top-6` on the inner div; with 9+ line rows the summary card top scrolls slightly above the viewport (bounding y = -76) - submit button remains visible so it is not blocking, but the stick offset is not perfectly pinned.

action_items: OPTIONAL: add a 'PO Date present' entry to the sidebar checklist. Today with PO Date cleared all 4 checklist items go green (item 4 short-circuits to ok when poDate is falsy) so 'Create Purchase Order in SAP' becomes enabled; clicking it correctly blocks with the toast 'PO Date is required' and does NOT open the dialog, but the green checklist is misleading.
OPTIONAL (design): replace native date inputs with the shadcn Calendar component for PO Date and line Delivery Date.
critical_code_review_comments: checklist item 4 (`!l.delivery_date || !poDate || ...`) treats an empty PO Date as valid, which is what lets canSubmit become true with no PO Date; validationErrors() catches it, so it is only a UI-state inconsistency, not a data risk.

PurchaseOrderPage.jsx is 580 lines and mixes state, search debouncing and 4 large card layouts; extracting the line-items table and summary sidebar into subcomponents would keep it under the maintainability threshold.
